 AFCON 2027 Qualifiers: The Greens Arrive in Lomé Ahead of Facing Togo this Tuesday 
 Sports 
 11/16/2026 - 16:42 
 The Algerian national football team arrived yesterday evening, Sunday, in the capital Lomé aboard a special flight, ahead of facing their Togolese counterparts scheduled for this Tuesday at Kégué Stadium (5:00 PM), as part of the fourth round (Group I) of the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON-2027) qualifiers.  
 The plane carrying the national team delegation, led by the Vice-President of the Algerian Football Federation (FAF), Mohamed El Amine Mesloug, landed at Gnassingbé Eyadéma International Airport in Lomé at 6:00 PM local time (7:00 PM Algerian time), after a four-and-a-half-hour flight, and the Algerian delegation was welcomed by the Ambassador of Algeria to Togo, Hocine Mezoued. 
 After completing the required procedures, The Greens headed to their place of residence, located about a quarter of an hour from the airport, to settle in and recover before the sole training session scheduled for this Monday on the main pitch of Kégué Stadium. 
 Following their victory in the first leg on Saturday evening in Tizi Ouzou (1-0), The Greens top the Group I standings with seven points, ahead of Zambia (4 points), Togo (3 points), and Burundi (2 points). 
 Achieving another victory tomorrow, Tuesday, in Lomé will allow the Algerian national team to formalize its qualification for the final stage of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, which will be jointly organized by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania.
